headline: India’s smartphone sale plunged 22% during festive season
body: The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

As rising memory costs have been pushing smartphone prices to a new height, the impact of it was quite visible during the just concluded Indian festive season (October 8–November 10) which collapsed by an estimated 22% year-over-year (YoY), noted Counterpoint. The rising phone prices pushed a weaker demand as buyers held back their purchases.

“The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales,” the findings said.

The research firm highlighted that festive discounts narrowed to 10–25%, from 35–40% in 2025. “Even discounted entry-level models were generally priced higher than a year ago, putting upgrades out of reach for many price-sensitive buyers. Brands instead leaned on no-cost EMIs, bank offers and trade-ins, with 48% of smartphone sales being finance-led.”

During the first wave (October 8–18), volumes fell 19% YoY, with online sales falling short of the performance seen during earlier sale events. Online sales, which account for a significant share of smartphone purchases, declined as higher consumer traffic failed to translate into actual conversions.

During festive season also, Samsung had the best of lot with a 21% share, overtaking Vivo, as its sales fell 8% YoY against a 22% market decline. Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S25 drew strong demand, while Samsung delayed price hikes until after the sales and managed inventory better than rivals.

Vivo and Oppo declined 21% and 24%, respectively, holding up better in mainline retail through retailer incentives and bundled offers, but were weaker online.

headline: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮 💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

headline: What to know about the online banking delays affecting major U.S. banks
body: Chase said that the technical problem was not the result of a cyberattack, stressing that it was an isolated incident and not related to anything other than a bug.
full_body:

A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused problems throughout the financial system on Monday (November 16, 2026), resulting in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle.

JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, said a software bug was affecting its internal hardware systems and causing transaction delays. The company was working to bring banking services back online.

Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

In a sense, yes. Customers at Bank of America, Citigroup and other banks trying to transact with Chase may have seen their transactions slow, even though those banks were not having issues with their services.

"Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," explained Joe Evangelisti, a spokesperson for Chase.

Zelle was not directly affected by the Chase glitch. But customers at other banks may have experienced transaction delays while trying to send or receive Zelle payments involving a Chase customer.

full_body:

India’s smartphone market dropped by 23.3% year-over-year (YoY ) during Q3 2026 to reach 36.8 million units shipments. It was the steepest quarterly contraction since Q4 2022 and also the weakest festive quarter in a decade, said IDC.

The research firm credited rising memory chip costs, pushed up by AI-driven demands , tightened component availability for the decline that led a very little room for vendors to hold prices.

Smartphone’s average selling price (ASP) was at a record high ($371), a 26% YoY growth, festive offers were a few, and due to that price-sensitive buyers held back purchases this season, and pressure is likely to carry into Q4 2026.

Samsung emerged as the top smartphone brand with a 17.7% share during Q3, followed by Vivo with a 16.8% share and Oppo having a 13.3% share. Vivo had a nearly 30% drop in shipments compared to Q3 2025, while Oppo’s fell by around 27%.

Apple stood at number four position with a 10.1% share, as the sharp decline across Chinese brands lifted its position in a shrinking market, even as Apple’s own shipments fell 25% YoY after a flat Q2.

Supply shortages on the iPhone 15, 16 and 17, along with price increases around the September launches, weighed on volumes, and less offers on older-generation iPhones cooled demand from aspirational buyers.

headline: Bank holiday for Chhath Puja on Monday? Check state-wise list of closures for November
body: Chhath Puja celebrations will continue until November 16, resulting in temporary bank closures in areas like Patna and Ranchi. However, digital banking will still be operational, ensuring clients can manage transactions online despite physical branch shutdowns during this festive season.

headline: India-Egypt trade has 'sky's the limit' potential, says Goyal; eyes bigger investments
body: India and Egypt are looking to significantly boost their trade partnership through enhanced cooperation and investment. headline: Bad air, bigger bills: Air pollution drives health insurance claims up fourfold in 3 years
body: In India, the demand for health insurance claims related to pollution has skyrocketed, witnessing a remarkable fourfold increase in just three years. Notably, working professionals between the ages of 31 and 55 constitute a significant 59% of these claims. Delhi tops the list for the highest claims, with other cities and smaller towns also reporting considerable figures.

“In another life, Jensen Huang might have been a teacher,” says Tae Kim in his book The Nvidia Way . Whether he likes it or not, the Nvidia co-founder’s reality has now been reset, forcing him back to his idiosyncratic style of solving problems: diagramming on a whiteboard. But this time he won’t get a clean start as the scandal-hit former chief of Nvidia will face intense scrutiny over his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who is at the centre of an alleged spy scandal.

Within days of reports emerging about Mr. Huang’s affair with Alice Huang , The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s head of healthcare and one of his direct reports. By then, the controversy had come to a head, forcing Mr. Huang to resign as CEO of Nvidia, the company he had built from scratch.

headline: Property seller takes Rs 5.22 lakh cash, faces tax penalty; why ITAT gave relief
body: The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) in Berhampur received information from the property registrar's office in Jharsuguda that the man had sold a property and collected Rs 5.22 lakh in cash as part of the payment. The registered sale deed also mentioned the cash component. Following this information, the AO issued the man a notice under Section 269SS of the Income Tax Act and levied a penalty under Section 271DA.
